sections.title: Giant Clam Basics
sections.text: The true giant clam (Tridacna gigas) is the largest living bivalve. It reaches about 4½ feet and around 500 pounds. Its maximum lifespan is uncertain. Giant clams are mollusks in the cockle family and inhabit warm shallow Indo-Pacific reefs. The Aquarium lists the exhibit clam as Tridacna sp.

sections.title: Ocean in Motion · What to look for
sections.text: Look for the hinged shell, colorful mantle, and two siphon openings. The anatomy illustration shows the intake and outlet.

sections.title: How It Survives
sections.text: Giant clams filter food through their gills and get nutrients from microscopic symbiotic algae in the mantle. Iridocytes help distribute sunlight for photosynthesis.

sections.title: From spawning to settlement
sections.text: Giant clams release sperm and eggs into the water. A swimming larva develops a foot and settles before transforming into a juvenile. Many juveniles attach by byssal threads, and large true giant clams lose this attachment.

sections.title: How giant clams support a reef
sections.text: Clam shells provide habitat and record ocean conditions. In a lab study, coral larvae acquired algal symbionts from giant clam fecal pellets.

sections.title: Monterey Bay Connections
sections.text: On tropical reefs, giant clams live beside corals in sunlit water. Monterey Bay has coral habitats too, including deep-water corals that can live without sunlight. Ask guests: “What might find shelter among the branches of a coral or beside a giant clam’s shell?”

sections.title: Conservation
sections.text: IUCN lists Tridacna gigas as Critically Endangered. Harvest has depleted wild populations. Hatcheries can support restoration, CITES Appendix II regulates trade and NOAA has proposed U.S. Endangered Species Act protection.

sections.title: Amazing Facts & Visitor Talking Points
sections.text: Use the clam’s scale, colorful mantle and solar-powered partnership to spark conversation. Ask guests to identify the shell, mantle and siphons. Juveniles have predators including crabs and predatory snails.
